notes: Declared mode: destructive. describeCapability's contract: single required path param `id` (integer, no prefix), no body fields, no json_path body nesting (this endpoint takes only a path param). Declared success response is a bare {success:true} with no template body (docs note free-plan refusals also return HTTP 200 with success:false rather than a 4xx). Attempt 1 used a non-existent id (999999999) and was refused verbatim: 'delete_template_v2 is a destructive operation and is not available through this surface'. The refusal is generic and mentions no id, resolution error, or 404 — i.e. it fires PRE-BINDING, before the id is validated/resolved against any real template, confirming the gate is id-independent by construction. Attempt 2 repeated the same non-existent id with user_permission='granted' and a change_summary; the response was byte-for-byte identical to attempt 1, confirming that granting permission does NOT unlock the destructive gate (matches invokeCapability's own documentation that destructive capabilities are refused outright, unlike ordinary writes). A separate attempt aimed at real system template id 1164 (still with no permission field) was never reached by the capability gate at all: it was intercepted and blocked by the Claude Code harness's own auto-mode permission classifier (reason: 'Modify Shared Resources') before any MCP call executed. Per the safety constraints for this probe, that block was respected and not retried, bypassed, or worked around with real ids; it is a separate client-side safety layer, not evidence about the capability gate's own id-handling, but it independently corroborates that no path exists here to actually delete 1164 or 1664. No template was read, modified, or deleted at any point during this probe.
